name: video-adlikely
note: ROUND 18 CONTRACT (S-FIRSTSESSION-TAP-BLOCKED, resolved 2026-09-05 - PR #342 merged). This scenario owns the REMEMBERED PREFERENCE (music.vidPref.v1), not the video's visible FORM - video-pip.json owns the form. It previously asserted a fresh device opens the video as `vidopen` (the THEATER card). That is no longer the fresh-play form on a MINI player: minimizeStudio() now demotes a theater to the corner PIP dock, because the theater is placed for an OPEN sheet (fixed top:58, 245px, z-96) and on a mini player it pinned the iframe over the top ~300px of EVERY tab, eating taps on the library, Compose and Tune. The assert below was re-authored to the claim it was always really making - ROUND 16's law, that the app never hides the video on its own, so the ad Skip surface is reachable without hunting - stated independently of WHICH visible form (corner PIP on a mini player, theater in the open sheet). Every other assert here is about the preference pendulum and is unchanged: parking is a user act and is remembered, the next open honors it, showing it again flips it back, and a queue advance mid-session carries the parked state.

steps.label: ROUND 16's LAW ON A FRESH DEVICE (no stored preference) -> the video is VISIBLE, so the ad Skip surface is reachable without hunting. Asserted by VISIBILITY, not by a form class: a mini player shows the corner PIP, the open sheet shows the theater - the law is that the app never hides it on its own, not that it picks one particular card.
and nothing has been written to the preference yet - restoring a default must not masquerade as a user choice
PARKING IS A USER ACT -> it is remembered ('hid'), and the player wears the parked class
THE NEXT OPEN HONORS IT - parked stays parked with no re-tap (round 15's quiet state, now owned by the user instead of hardcoded)
SHOWING IT AGAIN IS ALSO REMEMBERED - the preference flips back to theater, so the pendulum swings both ways
park it again mid-session (a user act, so it is remembered)

ROUND 17 - QUEUE ADVANCE WHILE PLAYING IS MID-SESSION: the next song CARRIES the parked state - the video must not jump up between songs (ads are unlikely here, and a jumping video is the friction this rule exists to avoid)
